title: Google Wins Antitrust Case, Is AI The Next Bubble? | The Friday Market Wrap!
summary: The September 5 wrap corrects a prior statement about the Federal Reserve, predicts the Supreme Court will uphold emergency tariffs, and interprets Google remedies and Apple policy risks. It then reviews software disruption, Broadcom demand and Lululemon product weakness, ending with a conditional AI-overinvestment scenario.
assessment: The clear adverse forecast is the predicted IEEPA win: the Supreme Court later ruled the statute did not authorize those tariffs. Google gained important remedy relief but did not win the underlying case. His AI-bust discussion is explicitly a scenario he was not yet worried about, not a crash prediction.
framework_points: Separate a statutory case from partisan assumptions.
Distinguish operating results from market expectations.
Watch whether cheaper technology weakens established moats.
Treat overinvestment as a conditional mechanism rather than a timed crash call.
transcript_cautions: At 60-82 seconds he corrects a prior Fed constitutional-amendment statement to the Federal Reserve Act of 1913. The earlier captured transcript lacks the erroneous wording, so the correction is documented without inventing a claim in that version.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman presents; speaker attribution follows the full dialogue.

claims.claim: The Fed was established by the Federal Reserve Act, correcting his earlier constitutional-amendment description.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Preserve the correction and the source-version limitation.
claims.reason: The reviewed Supreme Court Cook opinion describes the statutory Federal Reserve structure. This is an explicit correction, not an unacknowledged repeated error.

evidence.title: Trump v. Cook stay decision
evidence.finding: The Court denied interim relief and required minimum notice and opportunity to respond. It protected the Fed for-cause framework but did not finally decide whether the alleged conduct supplied cause. Neither conviction nor indictment was made an automatic prerequisite.

claims.next_check: Preserve the correction and the source-version limitation.

claims.claim: Weak employment news increases expectations of Fed easing.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare priced paths before and after the release.
claims.reason: A change in expectations needs a contemporaneous futures comparison; weak labor data do not by themselves commit the Fed to a cut.
claims.next_check: Compare priced paths before and after the release.

claims.claim: The Supreme Court will hear the tariff dispute, with a decision no earlier than December.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Record the docket and decision date.
claims.reason: The case reached the Court and was decided February 20, 2026, consistent with the earliest-date qualification.

evidence.title: Learning Resources and V.O.S. tariff decision
evidence.finding: The litigation reached the Supreme Court, which held that IEEPA did not authorize the tariffs. The opinion recounts the lower-court proceedings.

claims.next_check: Record the docket and decision date.

claims.claim: The Supreme Court will uphold the tariffs because Republican justices will defer to the president.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Use the dispositive holding, not subsequent replacement tariffs.
claims.reason: The Court held IEEPA did not authorize the tariffs. The political-deference explanation did not predict the actual statutory outcome.

evidence.title: Learning Resources and V.O.S. tariff decision
evidence.finding: The litigation reached the Supreme Court, which held that IEEPA did not authorize the tariffs. The opinion recounts the lower-court proceedings.

claims.next_check: Use the dispositive holding, not subsequent replacement tariffs.

claims.claim: Other statutory powers provide backup tariff options if IEEPA fails.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track the authority, limits and actual replacement measures.
claims.reason: The administration invoked Section 122 following the defeat. This supports availability of alternatives, not equivalence in scope, duration or legality.

evidence.title: Temporary import surcharge
evidence.finding: The administration invoked Section 122 after the IEEPA decision, confirming an alternative statutory avenue without making all tariff powers unlimited.

claims.next_check: Track the authority, limits and actual replacement measures.

claims.claim: Google effectively won the search antitrust case because it avoided the severe requested remedies.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Separate liability, requested remedies and ordered remedies.
claims.reason: Avoiding breakup and a blanket payment ban is meaningful remedy relief, but monopolization liability, exclusivity restrictions and data-sharing obligations remained.

evidence.title: Google search remedies
evidence.finding: The remedies included prohibitions on exclusive distribution contracts and mandatory data and syndication access. The monopolization liability finding remained; relief from a requested breakup was not complete victory in the case.

claims.next_check: Separate liability, requested remedies and ordered remedies.

claims.claim: Apple tariff risk has been removed because its products are exempt.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Check product, origin and every applicable tariff authority.
claims.reason: Product exclusions from reciprocal tariffs did not remove every other applicable tariff program. The official tariff schedule distinguishes overlapping authorities and exemptions.

evidence.title: 2025 tariff requirements
evidence.finding: USMCA origin rules provide exemptions from specified tariffs, while sectoral Section 232 duties and other rules must be evaluated separately.

claims.next_check: Check product, origin and every applicable tariff authority.

claims.claim: Apple needs a more credible AI strategy to regain a stronger growth narrative.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Specify adoption, monetization, margins and the expected re-rating horizon.
claims.reason: This is an investment judgment without a measurable product or valuation threshold.
claims.next_check: Specify adoption, monetization, margins and the expected re-rating horizon.

claims.claim: Kraft Heinz separation may not happen, especially given Buffett opposition.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track formal separation status and documented board rationale.
claims.reason: Work on the split was later paused, consistent with doubt about execution. The source states a possibility, not a firm cancellation forecast, and the pause does not prove Buffett caused it.

evidence.title: Kraft Heinz pauses separation
evidence.finding: The company paused work on the proposed separation and redirected resources to operating improvement. A pause is not permanent cancellation.

claims.next_check: Track formal separation status and documented board rationale.

claims.claim: Conglomerate formation and breakups can enrich advisers without necessarily improving the underlying businesses.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare operating outcomes and total fees with a transaction-specific counterfactual.
claims.reason: This is a warning about incentives, not a claim that all such transactions destroy value.
claims.next_check: Compare operating outcomes and total fees with a transaction-specific counterfactual.

claims.claim: Salesforce results are interpreted negatively because expectations and fears about its moat matter more than headline growth alone.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare forward revisions, retention and multiple changes.
claims.reason: A market narrative does not identify the separate contributions of guidance, valuation and AI fears.
claims.next_check: Compare forward revisions, retention and multiple changes.

claims.claim: Cheaper AI software creation may undermine the predictability and pricing power of established subscription vendors.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track churn, renewal pricing and actual replacement deployments.
claims.reason: Development cost is only one barrier; integration, data, distribution, trust and switching costs also matter. The transcript proposes a mechanism rather than demonstrating realized displacement.
claims.next_check: Track churn, renewal pricing and actual replacement deployments.

claims.claim: Broadcom custom-AI orders indicate strong demand, and the unnamed new customer is probably OpenAI.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Verify the counterparty and revenue conversion through issuer disclosures.
claims.reason: The customer identification is attributed to outside analysts, not established by the unnamed order disclosure. Orders are not all current recognized revenue.
claims.next_check: Verify the counterparty and revenue conversion through issuer disclosures.

claims.claim: Lululemon US weakness reflects merchandise execution, not only tariffs.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track product changes, traffic, conversion and regional comps.
claims.reason: The issuer acknowledged product-execution problems and Americas comparable sales fell 4%. Global comps rose 1%; the regional distinction matters.

evidence.title: Lululemon Q2 2025 results
evidence.finding: Americas comparable sales fell 4%, while global comparable sales rose 1%. Management acknowledged US product-execution problems alongside tariffs.

claims.next_check: Track product changes, traffic, conversion and regional comps.

claims.claim: Fashion risk makes long-term retailer leadership fragile.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Test brand durability through share, repeat buying and full-cycle margins.
claims.reason: His household observation is anecdotal, and the claim has no universal failure deadline.
claims.next_check: Test brand durability through share, repeat buying and full-cycle margins.

claims.claim: If AI improvements and monetization disappoint after huge capital spending, the industry could enter a digestion phase like telecom after 2000.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track incremental customer revenue, utilization, funding and capex revisions under defined thresholds.
claims.reason: He explicitly describes a possibility and says he is not worried yet. No trigger level or deadline is supplied, so this is not a forecast of an imminent crash.
claims.next_check: Track incremental customer revenue, utilization, funding and capex revisions under defined thresholds.

claims.claim: Reported disappointment with GPT-5 relative to GPT-4 raises questions about returns on ever-larger AI investment.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare task-specific capability, inference cost and realized economic value.
claims.reason: He attributes the technical assessment to critics and disclaims expertise. A benchmark or economic-return conclusion is not established by that report.
claims.next_check: Compare task-specific capability, inference cost and realized economic value.
